PullRequest.Title: sessions: add opt-in local isolation to the environment picker

Fixes #343629

## Summary

Adds the opt-in experimental setting `sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPickerLocalIsolation` (default: `false`). When enabled, the desktop Agents window offers **Local Folder** and **Local Worktree** in Environment instead of This Computer, and hides the separate Branch / New Worktree isolation control for new local sessions. The branch selector remains available.

The selected isolation is applied to the existing draft and replacement drafts after workspace or harness changes. Existing provider configuration APIs and schema helpers are reused. Unsupported worktree destinations are excluded, worktrees require a workspace, and Cloud, remote, and Dev Container flows retain their existing controls. Accessibility help documents the new choices.

## How to Test

Enable these settings in the desktop Agents window:

```json
{
  "sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled": true,
  "sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout": true,
  "sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPicker": true,
  "sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPickerLocalIsolation": true
}
```

Choose a local Git workspace, expand session options, and switch between Local Folder and Local Worktree. Verify the isolation control is absent, the branch selector remains, and changing the choice preserves the draft. Disable the new setting to restore the existing controls.

- Live isolated Agents window — visually inspected; pointer selection of Local Folder and keyboard selection of Local Worktree verified. Separate isolation controls: **0**; branch controls: **1**.
- No agent request was sent; full integration and smoke suites were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added awaited call, its one-per-draft call path, and the downstream resolveSessionConfig RPC are directly traced. Repository provider code proves new drafts are seeded to remembered isolation or worktree, making same-value calls realistic. Exact RPC duration varies by agent host, so severity is low rather than suppressing the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host resolveSessionConfig RPCs and the associated config serialization/work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Adds one serialized agent-host config-resolution round trip for every local draft creation or replacement, including repeated replacements after workspace or harness changes; the work is redundant whenever the fresh draft's seeded isolation already equals the selected environment.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased local draft creation/replacement latency because the composer awaits the extra RPC before the scenario can complete.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Creating or replacing a local draft performed the provider's normal initial configuration resolution only; NewChatWidget did not issue a second isolation mutation after openNewSession returned.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After every successful local draft creation, the added await unconditionally calls setIsolationMode for both Local Folder and Local Worktree, even if the provider's freshly resolved config already contains that effective isolation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 1462 always awaits provider.setIsolationMode after openNewSession whenever a local isolation environment is selected; there is no equality check against provider.getSessionConfig before this call.
Findings.Title: Skip isolation updates when the draft already has that mode
Findings.Impact: With the opt-in enabled, selecting Local Worktree (the provider's default) or recreating a draft whose seeded isolation matches the current picker choice incurs an avoidable agent-host round trip on the critical path of opening/replacing the draft. This repeats once per workspace or harness-driven replacement.
Findings.Evidence: BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.setIsolationMode first waits for the draft config, then _setTransientNewSessionConfigValues always calls _refreshNewSessionConfig, which invokes connection.resolveSessionConfig. The provider seeds new local drafts from remembered workspace isolation or defaults to worktree in _initialNewSessionConfig, so Local Worktree commonly already matches; similarly a remembered folder can match Local Folder. Even in those matching cases this line forces a second serialized resolve after the existing initial resolve.
Findings.Recommendation: After the initial config is available, compare the effective isolation with the requested mode and skip the mutation when they match; the safest bounded location is setIsolationMode itself, since it already obtains the resolved config before issuing the refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or replace a local draft with Local Folder/Local Worktree selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: openNewSession creates the replacement draft, then the added setIsolationMode await must finish before _createSessionNow returns and workspace/harness reconciliation can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial agent-host session-config discovery via resolveSessionConfig
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial resolution per fresh local draft, with a possible second initialization request only when normalization requires it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Draft creation returned without NewChatWidget waiting for and following the initial config resolution with an isolation mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously background/provider-owned; the new post-create setter waits for this initial resolution before it can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply isolation and re-resolve the draft configuration via setIsolationMode -> _refreshNewSessionConfig -> connection.resolveSessionConfig
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added call per successful local draft creation/replacement, including when seeded isolation already matches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No post-open isolation RPC was issued by NewChatWidget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialized after initial resolution and awaited before draft creation/replacement completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of local draft creations and workspace/provider/harness-driven draft replacements; no collection fan-out after provider selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The added mutation is serialized after openNewSession and after any current config resolution; provider state prevents parallel resolution for this call path. Replacements are cancellation-managed, so effective cardinality is one added mutation per completed replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The draft schema/config is cached after initial resolution and isolation is seeded from remembered workspace state or a worktree default, but setIsolationMode does not use the cached effective value to no-op a matching request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed await and downstream unconditional resolveSessionConfig call are directly traced, and provider initialization proves matching seeded values are realistic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact resolveSessionConfig latency depends on the local agent host and authentication/startup state; the extra serialized RPC and matching-value trigger are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated IPC on matching-value creations; changing isolation when values differ is required feature work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch Local Folder/Local Worktree on an existing uncreated draft
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The environment picker awaits setIsolationMode before committing the selected environment and announcing the change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve agent-host draft configuration with the newly selected isolation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per actual picker switch; same-environment selections return before this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Isolation was changed through the separate repository config picker rather than the Environment picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the picker selection until the host confirms the config.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User environment switches, normally one call per deliberate selection rather than per provider or workspace item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A selection is awaited; the provider waits for any current config resolution before starting the next one, bounding effective resolution concurrency per draft.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current config is cached and drives the selected environment; the early ID equality guard avoids same-selection calls on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary and ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host response time varies, but call cardinality is one and the mutation is necessary when switching modes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the one RPC applies a genuinely changed isolation and has bounded cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and reconcile Environment options in the new-session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous observable derivations filter the registered providers, resolve the selected workspace/provider from cached provider state, and render the picker; no filesystem, network, subprocess, or database operation is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered session providers and environment choices, both small effective collections; local isolation adds one extra local option.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI derivation; configuration-event equality suppresses downstream recomputation when the four-setting result is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getSessionConfig is a synchronous cached read for the uncreated draft owned by NewChatWidget; workspace/provider resolution uses provider-held state. No new cache or negative-cache lifecycle is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High after tracing observableFromEvent equality and provider config ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider count varies, but the added linear filtering and tiny allocations are not plausibly material.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable rendering, layout, or allocation regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh repository controls when the experimental settings change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A relevant setting change rebuilds menu registrations for visible sessions synchronously; this is off normal input/render hot paths and occurs only on setting changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible session count and schema property count. The diff adds constant-time setting checks and one property exclusion inside the existing loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single event-handler refresh; no async work or fan-out beyond the existing visible-session loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing session configs are read through the same provider cache as before; the diff does not introduce a new config subscription on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large session grids increase existing menu rebuild cost, but the incremental work is constant and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression from the added setting predicates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Sessions accessibility help with local isolation enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Builds one additional localized string in memory when accessibility help content is requested; no external boundary lies on the path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant-size content, independent of sessions or workspaces.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous help-content build per invocation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 9 changed files and traced draft creation, picker mutation, observable rendering, menu refresh, and accessibility-help paths. Submitted one low-severity finding for an unconditional matching-value isolation update that adds a serialized agent-host config RPC to local draft creation/replacement.
